note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with a 2-3 day history of wheezing, cough, shortness of breath, and fever consistent with an asthma flare.
- History of childhood asthma, hay fever, and eczema; currently using salbutamol inhaler intermittently; management plan includes increased inhaler use, prescription for spacer and peak flow meter, and follow-up review.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Asthma exacerbation  
- Symptoms started 2-3 days ago with wheezing, cough (non-productive), shortness of breath on exertion, difficulty completing sentences, and low-grade fever (~37°C). No chest pain or hemoptysis. No nocturnal symptoms reported.  
- History of childhood asthma with intermittent hospital admissions, ceased regular inhalers 3-4 years ago, currently uses salbutamol inhaler occasionally (every few weeks, some use with exercise).  
- No smoking history; hay fever present but untreated.  
- Unable to exercise or walk to work currently; working from home or on sick leave.  
- Physical examination and vitals not documented beyond temperature.  
- Differential includes viral respiratory infection triggering asthma exacerbation or pollen/allergen exposure.  
- Plan: Increase salbutamol use (2-4 puffs every 4 hours), start regular antihistamines for hay fever, prescribe spacer and peak flow meter, monitor peak flow twice daily for one week, follow-up phone review in one week to assess control and consider further medication. Immediate re-contact advised if fever worsens or wheezing deteriorates.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
- No medications currently taken for hay fever

Allergies:
- None reported

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (childhood and adult, intermittent hospital admissions)  
- Hay fever  
- Eczema

Social History:
- Lives with partner  
- Engineer by occupation  
- Non-smoker  
- Drinks one glass of wine every 2-3 days

Preventative History:
- Not discussed

Physical Examination:
- Temperature reported approximately 37°C by patient  
- No other examination findings documented

Plan:
- Prescribe spacer and peak flow meter; pharmacist to provide usage instructions  
- Advise increased frequency of salbutamol inhaler (2-4 puffs every 4 hours)  
- Advise starting regular antihistamine for hay fever symptoms  
- Patient to record peak flow readings morning and evening for 1 week  
- Arrange follow-up phone review in one week to review peak flow values and symptoms  
- Immediate contact if fever rises or wheezing worsens  
- Consider initiation of additional asthma medications depending on review findings
